questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the TTL field in an IP datagram?

options.text: To ensure data integrity during transmission
To prevent packets from looping indefinitely
To prioritize packets based on importance
To encrypt data for secure transmission

questions.explanation: The TTL field limits the number of hops a packet can take, thus preventing it from circulating indefinitely in the network. This mechanism helps to avoid routing loops.

questions.stem: What happens to an IP packet when its TTL reaches zero?

options.text: It is forwarded to the next router
It is discarded
It is returned to the sender
It is stored in a buffer

questions.explanation: When the TTL of an IP packet reaches zero, the packet is discarded to prevent it from looping indefinitely in the network. This is a safeguard against routing loops.

questions.stem: A packet with an initial TTL of 10 traverses 7 routers. What is the TTL when it reaches the last router? Provide your answer as an integer.
questions.explanation: Each router decrements the TTL by 1. Starting with a TTL of 10 and subtracting 7 for the routers gives a final TTL of 3.

questions.stem: Explain how the traceroute utility works and what information it provides.
markingGuide: Traceroute sends packets with incrementally increasing TTL values.
Each router along the path decrements the TTL and, when it reaches zero, sends an ICMP Time Exceeded message back to the sender.
Traceroute records the time taken for each hop and identifies the routers in the path to the destination.
questions.explanation: Traceroute helps map the path packets take to a destination by sending packets with increasing TTL values. Each router sends back an ICMP message when the TTL reaches zero, allowing traceroute to identify the path and measure the time taken for each hop.

questions.stem: Describe the process of how a device uses ARP to communicate with another device on the same local network.
markingGuide: The device broadcasts an ARP request on the local network.
The ARP request asks for the MAC address corresponding to a specific IP address.
The device with the matching IP address responds with an ARP reply, providing its MAC address.
questions.explanation: When a device wants to communicate with another device on the same network, it uses ARP to resolve the IP address to a MAC address. The device broadcasts an ARP request, and the target device responds with its MAC address.
